source: Build an obby where players climb a tower of floating blocks and platforms to reach a flag at the top.

answers.ask: What should the tower look like - candy-coloured blocks, grimy industrial, floating fantasy islands?
answers.answer: Use a simple colourful cartoon obby look: bright floating blocks and platforms against a clear sky.

answers.ask: How tall is the tower? That decides whether it can be framed in one pass.
answers.answer: Make it a small tower, roughly 12–15 platform jumps tall, so the full climb can be framed in one pass.

answers.ask: Should there be checkpoints on the way up, or does falling send you back to the bottom?
answers.answer: Include a few checkpoints along the way up so falling does not always send players back to the bottom.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: What should the tower look like - candy-coloured blocks, grimy industrial, floating fantasy islands? A: Use a simple colourful cartoon obby look: bright floating blocks and platforms against a clear sky.
- [author] scale — Q: How tall is the tower? That decides whether it can be framed in one pass. A: Make it a small tower, roughly 12–15 platform jumps tall, so the full climb can be framed in one pass.
- [author] goal — Q: Should there be checkpoints on the way up, or does falling send you back to the bottom? A: Include a few checkpoints along the way up so falling does not always send players back to the bottom.
- [agent_inferred] checkpoint count — Q: How many does “a few” mean for this short climb? A: Use three checkpoints, spaced across the 12–15 jumps.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a small colorful cartoon obby tower rising through roughly 12–15 jumps made from bright floating blocks and platforms against a clear sky. Arrange one ordered upward route with physics-legal gaps and safe landings. Place three clearly visible checkpoint pads at roughly even intervals through the climb. Finish with one distinct top platform carrying a single flag, and keep the entire base-to-flag route readable in one framed view.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Obby & Platformer.

## Shape and preset
Use `course-tower`: the floating platform route stacks vertically to the top flag. Use the Classic Obby preset with its shape replaced by the authored tower, retaining its ordered jumps and checkpoints, dropping moving platforms, and adding the top winner area.

## Config requirements
Use `path-track` for the ordered chain of roughly 12–15 floating platform jumps. Use `obstacle-jump` for the bright block-to-block transfers. Use the visible half of `checkpoint-respawn` as three safe pads. Use the visible half of `winner-zone` as one top platform with a single flag.

## Layout requirements
Place exactly three `checkpoint-respawn` points on the three safe pads, spaced across the lower, middle, and upper portions of the climb. Place one `winner-zone` at the top flag platform. No moving obstacles, timed blocks, collectibles, or contact-lethal surfaces are required.

## Layout components
The build is one compact vertical tower containing roughly 12–15 floating jumps, three checkpoint pads, one safe base, and one flag platform at the top. Platforms overlap vertically and remain within standard avatar jump limits. Compose the full sequence so every landing and checkpoint is identifiable.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: linked level plans must establish a physics-valid jump chain before the colorful isometric tower is dressed.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is small, explicitly limited to roughly 12–15 jumps. The theme is simple bright cartoon blocks against clear sky. Use `P6` because the route must be valid by construction and `P2` because floating platforms stack above one another.
